section_summary: This final section concludes the American Embassy in Mexico City’s memorandum on records recovered from the former Japanese Embassy and reproduces numerous enclosures, including correspondence, coded telegrams, Japanese alien-control regulations, an appeal for Japanese intervention in the European war, an unusual German transit request, a Sino-Japanese treaty note, and encrypted diplomatic traffic. It then presents an FBI-supplied analysis of former Japanese minister Kiyoshi Yamagata’s diary, emphasizing Japanese propaganda, political contacts, and suspected espionage in Chile. The closing documents concern archives seized from the former Japanese Embassy in Brazil, including a list of 112 prospective repatriates and a French report on China’s Blue Shirts Society, followed by a State Department transmission to Nanking.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on miscellaneous papers of the former Japanese Embassy in Mexico City (conclusion)
subfiles.from: Tien Yuen Chang, Edward Osborne Coote, Grigori Kasparov, and Walter J. Linthicum
subfiles.about: Concludes an inter-Allied review of miscellaneous records recovered from the former Japanese Embassy in Mexico City.
subfiles.summary: Concluding inventory of Mexico City Japanese Embassy papers: associations in Argentina, arms exports to Mexico, a property deed, consular rules, secret funds in Peru, a compromised State trade instruction and The Colorado Times; signed by four embassies.

subfiles.title: Reply to Elena Cornejo concerning toothbrush-manufacturing machinery
subfiles.from: Thomas H. Lockett, Commercial Attaché, American Embassy
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Cornejo’s request for the names and addresses of manufacturers of toothbrush-making machinery.
subfiles.summary: Commercial Attaché acknowledges Elena Cornejo's May 19 letter and invites her to ask for Thomas Webber at the Embassy.

subfiles.title: Request for information on toothbrush-manufacturing machinery
subfiles.to: Consul General of the United States of America
subfiles.about: Requests contacts for a simple, low-capital machine suitable for a small family toothbrush factory.
subfiles.summary: Cornejo asks for names of toothbrush-machinery manufacturers or agents in the US for a small family enterprise.

subfiles.title: Coded telegram from Hermosillo to the Japanese Minister at Mérida
subfiles.about: A Mexican telegraph form carries a largely encoded message addressed to the Japanese Minister at Mérida.
subfiles.summary: Coded telegram from Hermosillo of June 2, 1925 to the Japanese Minister at Mérida, mostly code groups ending with TAITO and YODOGAWA.

subfiles.title: Coded cable to the Japanese Consul in Los Angeles
subfiles.about: A commercial cable form records an extensive encoded message sent from Mexico to the Japanese consul in Los Angeles.
subfiles.summary: Coded cable to the Japanese Consul in Los Angeles; almost entirely cipher groups.

subfiles.title: Regulations for enforcing the decree on entry, residence, and departure of aliens from Japan
subfiles.to: Japanese diplomatic posts and domestic authorities
subfiles.about: Sets out procedures and forms governing the entry, residence, travel, registration, and expulsion of aliens in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese-language regulation implements the April 13, 1939 decree controlling foreigners’ entry into, residence in, and departure from Japan. It discusses official scrutiny, landing permission, residence registration, movements, travel documents, fees, and expulsion orders. The final pages reproduce prescribed forms, stamps, residence certificates, travel certificates, and departure orders.

subfiles.title: Circular defining exceptions for foreign diplomats and their households
subfiles.from: Japanese Foreign Ministry and Home Ministry Security Bureau
subfiles.to: Overseas diplomatic posts and prefectural authorities
subfiles.about: Defines diplomatic, consular, family, and household categories exempted from parts of the April 13 alien-control decree.
subfiles.summary: The circular supplements the April 13, 1939 regulations by addressing foreign diplomatic and consular personnel and their families and servants. It enumerates ambassadors, ministers, consular officials, military and naval attachés, commercial officials, couriers, interpreters, domestic employees, and related household members. The text seeks reciprocal treatment and coordination between the Foreign and Home Ministries.

subfiles.title: Higinio Álvarez’s proposal for Japanese attacks on British and French possessions
subfiles.about: Urges Japan to exploit the European war by attacking Britain and France in Asia and offers to seek German support.
subfiles.summary: Higinio Álvarez proposes Japan exploit the European war to attack British and French possessions, seizing Australia, Malaya, Singapore and Indochina, offering to approach Germany and suggesting Germany keep Russia neutral.

subfiles.title: German request to conceal Alois Ecker from a passenger list
subfiles.from: J. Fritz von Collenberg, German Minister in Mexico
subfiles.about: Requests Japanese assistance allowing Alois Ecker to sail without appearing on the passenger list or, failing that, to receive help from the ship’s captain.
subfiles.summary: German Legation asks that musician Alois Ecker, returning via Japan on the Hie Maru after avoiding US military service, be hidden from the Los Angeles passenger list; annotated as refused.

subfiles.title: German request for a Japanese transit visa for Alois Ecker
subfiles.about: Requests a Japanese transit visa for German musician Alois Ecker.
subfiles.summary: German Legation requests a Japanese transit visa for Ecker, stating he has no defense connection and no prior punishment.

subfiles.title: Transit-visa information form for Alois Ecker
subfiles.about: Records personal and passport information supporting Ecker’s transit request.
subfiles.summary: Transit-visa form for Alois Ecker, German musician born at Wels on February 1, 1896, single.

subfiles.title: Japanese rejection of China’s unilateral abrogation of the 1915 treaties and notes
subfiles.about: Rejects China’s attempt to cancel the Sino-Japanese treaties and notes of 1915.
subfiles.summary: Japan rejects China's unilateral abrogation of the 1915 treaties as validly concluded, cites Paris and Washington conferences, refuses further changes and rejects proposals on Port Arthur and Dairen.

subfiles.title: Register or packet of encrypted Japanese diplomatic telegrams
subfiles.from: Japanese diplomatic offices, including Mexico City
subfiles.to: Japanese Foreign Ministry and other coded stations
subfiles.about: Contains numbered, encrypted diplomatic messages and transmission records, including a signed cable from Mexico City to Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: The enclosure consists of numerous numbered cipher messages dated principally February 16–17, with routing codes, time stamps, letter groups, and numerical groups. One legible cover message is dated January 14, 1938, addressed from Mexico City to the Foreign Minister in Tokyo, and signed Koshida. The substantive contents cannot be recovered from the encrypted text alone.

subfiles.title: FBI letter transmitting an analysis of Kiyoshi Yamagata’s diary
subfiles.from: John Edgar Hoover, Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.to: Frederick B. Lyon, Department of State
subfiles.about: Forwards a British analysis of the diary of former Japanese Minister to Chile Kiyoshi Yamagata.
subfiles.summary: Hoover sends a British-source memorandum analyzing Kiyoshi Yamagata's diary, also given to the Santiago Embassy and to naval and military intelligence.

subfiles.title: Analysis of the diary of Kiyoshi Yamagata
subfiles.from: British source in Santiago, transmitted through the FBI
subfiles.to: United States intelligence and diplomatic officials
subfiles.about: Profiles the Chilean and Japanese political, journalistic, business, and espionage contacts named in Yamagata’s August 1942 diary.
subfiles.summary: Analysis of Yamagata's diary from the Santiago Legation archives profiles journalists, politicians and agents aiding Japanese propaganda and intelligence, including efforts to preserve Chilean neutrality and cultivate Arturo Alessandri.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 232: Documents contained in locked safes and filing cabinets of the former Japanese Embassy
subfiles.about: Transmits a Legal Attaché’s memorandum giving further information on records recovered from the former Japanese Embassy in Brazil.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 232 answers Airgram A-384 with a Legal Attaché memorandum on identification cards, registrations, repatriation records, the Blue Shirts and old cables from the Rio Embassy safes.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on the archives of the Japanese Embassy in Rio de Janeiro
subfiles.to: United States Ambassador in Brazil, attention H. V. Blocker
subfiles.about: Evaluates selected categories of material recovered from the former Japanese Embassy archives in Brazil.
subfiles.summary: Papich finds Rio's identity and membership cards of little intelligence value; notes 112 repatriation forms, a document on China's Blue Shirts Society and cable copybooks from about 1897-1910.

subfiles.title: List of repatriates from the former Japanese Embassy records in Brazil
subfiles.from: Former Japanese Embassy records, Rio de Janeiro
subfiles.about: Lists 112 people identified on forms as prospective Japanese repatriates.
subfiles.summary: The two-page attachment supplies the names corresponding to 112 filled-in repatriation forms found in the Embassy archives. The accompanying memorandum states that the forms contained limited biographical information, lacked repatriation dates, and produced no significant results when checked against American files.

subfiles.title: French report on the secret Blue Shirts association in China
subfiles.about: Describes the origins, fascist orientation, leadership, and military influence of China’s Blue Shirts Society.
subfiles.summary: French report on the Blue Shirts: a secret fascist organization tied to Kuomintang conflicts and Chiang Kai-shek's young officers, whose members held influential government and army posts.

subfiles.title: Transmission of translated documents on the Blue Shirts and anti-Japanese activity
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge of the American Mission, Nanking
subfiles.about: Sends translated copies of documents entitled “Blue Shirts” and “Anti-Japanese Activity” for the Embassy’s information.
subfiles.summary: Department transmits translated Rio documents on the Blue Shirts, a Chinese anti-Japanese group, noting the Embassy found no Falange connection.
